newsitem.title: USA: Apple revamps board of directors.
newsitem.headline: Apple revamps board of directors.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc cofounder Steve Jobs said Wednesday the company revamped its entire board of directors, naming four new board members -- including Jobs.
Jobs also told the MacWorld Conference here that three board members, including early financier and one-time chairman A.C. Mike Markkula, resigned.

The new board members include Oracle Corp Chairman Larry Ellison, one-time International Business Machines Corp Chief Financial Officer Jerry York, Intuit Inc president William Campbell, and Jobs, the cofounder who returned to the company in December as part-time strategic advisor.
"We're adding a tremedous amount of industry expertise," Jobs told Apple customers and investors at the the trade show.

Apple had been criticized for not having enough members with a deep understanding of the computer business. Investors had also griped that the board was not willing to consider a radical new strategy for the ailing computer company.
Jobs said the company would not name a new chairman at this time, leaving open the question whether he himself will take the position.
The recently vacated post of chief executive also remains unfilled.
